subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an operator-configurable user-output file permission policy, and if so which write surfaces are allowed to honor it?
rationale: The request adds config surface and intentionally changes filesystem access boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary between user-facing output and private OpenClaw state.

options.title: Approve a narrow user-output policy
options.body: Add a constrained config surface that applies only to user-facing workspace/tool artifacts, with tests proving private config, credential, state, session, and auth paths stay restrictive.

options.title: Keep fixed defaults and document deployment policy
options.body: Leave runtime permissions fixed and document Docker/NAS ACL or service-umask recipes for shared-output deployments.

options.title: Defer into broader permission design
options.body: Keep this open until related media and state permission issues settle into one coherent filesystem policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add a constrained config surface that applies only to user-facing workspace/tool artifacts, with tests proving private config, credential, state, session, and auth paths stay restrictive.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history signal is recent sandbox/apply_patch permission hardening, and that area likely needs to anchor the security boundary decision.
